core_requests: P275 c1: core ctx.tls handshake helper (v3lum.core.tls, P329/WP25) returning the DER chain even when verification fails (read-only capture context, verification result kept separately), plus a FakeTls in tests/fakes.py; until then tls_inspect adapts ctx.net.connect + ctx.net.wrap_tls (verifying only: failed chains are reported from the verify error alone)

P347 c6 / P275 c8: a module-facing accessor for the entity's case-graph tags (e.g. ctx.case_tags() / ctx.hostile()) instead of reading runtime.policy_context.graph

P347 c3: a capture-scoped LIGHT binding that lets ctx.http fetch the redirect targets (and their same-host assets) of the same capture, re-checked by the SSRF and hostile-host guards; today assets on hosts other than the seed are refused (seed binding)
P078 c6: a shared core helper for recipient-URL redaction (v3lum.core.redact.redact_recipient_url); url_unwrap.redact_url_values + redact.redact_url are used now

P078: config.KNOWN_KEYS does not list urldna/urlquery (cond 4 says it should); the keys are registered through the provider fragments (urldna.json, urlquery.json) and resolve through config.key_registry
P275 c8: a correlation rule (typosquat pack, WP24) over the new attribute tls_phishing_signals

P347 c9: report/html.py (and the terminal summary) render the attribute page_screenshot {data_uri, caption, sha256} as an embedded (CSP img-src data:, JPEG data URI <= 1.5 MB, the module already enforces the size) with its caption under it; today no renderer reads it
notes: P078 is implemented as two PASSIVE modules in one file: url_scanners_third_party (urlDNA + urlquery, terms key-terms, tier community, as the council decided) and url_scanners_lookyloo (CIRCL Lookyloo; registry source circl.lookyloo is 'unknown' until legal records CIRCL's terms, cond 5, so it is a separate module to keep the key-terms class). The council's group label opsec=light could not be kept for P078: after c1/c2 nothing touches the target and contract v2 makes LIGHT <=> disclosure target (LIGHT ctx.http binds the first hop to the seed and refuses credential headers), so both are disclosure third_party with run_on='seeds' and default_enabled=False. No submission/scan request can be built (build_request guard + core forbidden_probe, test-asserted); Sucuri/Web-Check/CheckPhish not implemented (c2, backlog). urlquery uses v2 (/public/v2/reports/search; v1 deprecated, its keyless 401 kept as a fixture); urlDNA uses 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' per its docs. tls_inspect: LIGHT, one handshake per host per case through ctx.net, interception detected in the single-handshake form (verified chain anchor outside certifi's Mozilla bundle, public targets only), findings ownership-scoped (own asset / in-scope keep severity, others INFO, hostile = facts + phishing signals), tls_certificate in the CR17 shape, shared_cert for CR31. page_capture: LIGHT, optional extra v3lum[capture] (playwright), the browser is a renderer only - every request is fulfilled through ctx.http by the route handler and Chromium's own network points at a closed loopback proxy; refuses as root, without proxy_light, for untagged seeds, pivots and recipient-token URLs without --confirm-url. Extras fragments cryptography.json (extra 'tls', optional, never required) and playwright.json (extra 'capture') were added; if another batch (p9-G13-1 tls_protocol_scan) adds cryptography.json too, keep one. Fixtures are the prep's documented/synthetic/observed files (documentation values only; no key or private key). Review 2026-11-26: Lookyloo captures carry capture_url/subject_role and only captures of the value pivot (live answers list captures of other sites that merely contain the host), duplicates dropped, a failed redirect read keeps the listed captures (partial); answering urlDNA/urlquery sources are reported ok/empty in source_statuses (coverage counted only failures before); OfflineError/DeadlineExceeded keep 'offline'/'timeout'; tls_inspect SAN pivots follow c9 on hostile hosts too and in-scope findings are tagged in_scope; page_capture refuses unless selected by name (c6: never through --preset deep), enforces the 30 s budget and the 10-hop navigation cap in the route handler and the driver (c5), and masks e-mails/recipient tokens in report URLs (c8; the evidence keeps them).
